note: ⌨️ The keyboard path of every generation3d editor verb a user repeats. It lists the chords THIS APP declares; the framework mints its own on top (`undo`/`redo` appear here because the app re-declares them, while the interaction domain's `escape`→`clearSelection` and `mod+a`→`selectAll` are minted by `build_definition` and are deliberately NOT this fixture's to state). A chord here MUST reach an ARG-FREE declared action: `ShellHost`'s keybinding loop fires an arg-free action straight through `onAction`, and opens a staged argument form for anything else — which is slower than the control the chord was meant to replace. A chord for a WINDOW-OWNED action (`windowScoped`) is live only while that window kind has focus, because the same handler builds its action lookup from the focused window kind alone; a chord token is matched against `event.key` verbatim, so punctuation is spelled as the character (`.`), never as a name (`period`). Both measured against the running playground, not inferred. `fitGraph` is deliberately absent: it is shell chrome over the node-graph surface, not an app action, and the shell binds `F` to it itself. Driven by `✏️editor/🧪️tests/🔬️unit/🦀️.rs` `the_editor_binds_every_keyboard_verb_the_fixture_names`; this file, not that test, is the statement.

bindings.why: History — the framework's own reserved verb.
History — the framework's own reserved verb.
Graph — remove what is selected, the chord three sibling artifacts already declare.

Preview — stop a running evaluation. The token is `.` and not `period` because ShellHost matches the last chord segment against event.key verbatim; window-scoped because cancelPreviewEval is owned by the preview window kinds.
Preview — step the shading ladder without reaching for the picker.
Generate — add a generation, the mode's primary create verb. Window-scoped: addGeneration is owned by the Generations window kind, so the chord is live while that window has focus.
IO — the chord every application in the world uses to open a file.
IO — export; carries a required format, so this chord opens the staged form on purpose.

shellChrome.why: Painted by the shell over any node-graph surface, not declared by this app — the app must NOT re-bind it.
